findings.finding: The complexity-counting protocol native_schema_supported(model_cls) is under-specified where it matters most: it says 'count OPTIONAL properties in model_cls.model_json_schema()' but never states the count must RECURSE into nested model / list-item / $defs schemas. The target contracts (VerificationOutput) have exactly ONE top-level property — `verifications: list[Verification]` — and all 22-36 optionals live nested inside Verification.severity_attributes and Verification.binary. A literal reading (count of the top-level `properties`) yields 1, never exceeds any bound, and silently leaves NativeOutput ON — reproducing the exact defect the plan is fixing.

scenarios: Executor implements the count against model_json_schema()['properties'] literally; every verification contract reports 1 optional, stays below the bound, keeps NativeOutput, and Bedrock 400s exactly as today — the fix ships inert

A reviewer of the implementation cannot tell from the plan whether a top-level or recursive count is intended, so the AC ('exceeds the measured bound') can be satisfied by a count that never fires on the real contracts

findings.checklist_item: State explicitly that the optional/union count is an intentional coarse over-approximation of grammar-compile cost (backstopped by the Part 3 fallback), and specify whether nested/$defs optionals are counted or only top-level properties.
evidence: Plan: 'counts OPTIONAL properties (and union-typed properties) in `model_json_schema()` and returns False above a conservative measured bound'
Plan's own measurement: 'descriptions stripped (8719->2403 B), NATIVE FAIL 59.8s' — shows byte size is not the driver, implying structural depth is, which a top-level optional count may not reflect
Mechanism is nonetheless defensible because Part 3's WARNING-logged single fallback to PROMPTED (proven 11.2s) catches any mis-prediction where a schema passes the gate but still 400s
findings.finding: Part 1's `native_schema_supported` predicate uses top-level OPTIONAL/union property count as a proxy for grammar-compilation cost, but the proven driver is total structural complexity (nested properties / $defs depth), which the count does not fully capture; the plan does not state that the count is an intentional coarse over-approximation nor whether nested optionals are counted.
findings.location: Approach, part 1 ('counts OPTIONAL properties (and union-typed properties) in model_json_schema()')
scenarios: A future/other contract with few top-level optional fields but deep nested objects passes the complexity gate as native-safe, then 400s at compile time — relying on the Part 3 fallback rather than being prevented by Part 1
findings.suggested_fix: In the Part 1 paragraph, add one sentence: 'The count is a deliberately coarse over-approximation of compile cost (the true driver is structural/nested complexity, not byte size — see the descriptions-stripped 59.8s FAIL); it counts optionals at [top-level only / recursively through $defs], and any schema that passes the gate yet still 400s is caught by the Part 3 fallback.'
